title: Hobbies Across the Loops
text: “Antiques are kind of hard to judge by this world’s standards, aren’t they?”
“If I recall, Fiancée and Queen both said that weapon the Three Heroes Church’s pope showed off was an antique too, I believe.”
“Ah, that certainly was an antique. A prized one, at that.”
Father chuckled softly at that.
“You handled it with plenty of room to spare, I recall.”
“Yeah, it was supposedly a pretty powerful weapon… but in front of a Hero, it turned out to be nothing much at all.”
“If anything, the items found on places like Cal Mira Island would’ve fetched quite a sum if sold, wouldn’t they?”
“Vof, it’s hard to feel satisfied about a hobby when Heroes are involved.”
And so the conversation about expensive hobbies rolled on.
“Oh, speaking of which, are there any memorable hobbies from other loops—me, or anyone else? I figure Motoyasu-kun’s is always Filolial-related, though.”
“Naturally, indeed.”

Beyond simply raising Filolial-samas, there was matchmaking and choosing the next generation to fulfill Yuki-chan’s wish of producing ever-faster racing wings—truly a deep and profound pursuit, I say.
“In the very first world, I believe Father’s hobby was accessory-making and compounding, along with keeping monsters.”
Father had taken care of the Raph-species, the very origin of Raph-chan, indeed.
“Ah… I think I’ve heard that one before. Gaelion-chan and Raph-chan both said something along those lines.”
This loop’s Father, however, showed little interest in Raph-chan.
“What about other loops? Something other than the Raph-species—or Raphtalia-chan-related stuff, I mean.”

Asked to recall, I tried. The Father from the very first loop I looped back to was already one who’d grown close with Big Sister. There was no Raph-species in that loop… but it seemed the other hobbies had continued much as before. So there wasn’t much difference there. Next was… ugh, the Father who’d devoted himself, body and soul, to Rival—what on earth was his hobby? It floated hazily in my memory… surely he hadn’t spent every waking moment doting on Rival. But—kuuu—the truth was, once I thought they were busy being lovey-dovey, I simply stopped watching much after that. I’d go visit now and then, chat about this and that… and otherwise traveled the world exactly as I pleased. And that’s Rival’s fault, I say! Still, at the very least, I recall he seemed fond of Panda and liked dressing her up. But beyond that, I couldn’t remember a thing.
“Gah… why couldn’t I have watched over that Father more closely!? I wanted to know more, I say!”
“What’s with that line? Sounds like some long-lived character regretting things at a comrade’s funeral. I mean, sure, you’ve looped a ridiculous number of times, Motoyasu-kun, but still.”
I intended to keep moving forward no matter how many regrets piled up—but that didn’t mean I claimed to feel no remorse at all, I say.
“Vof, the heart of living without regret, as taught by Spear Hero.”
“I won’t allow that.”
“There are clearly things one should and shouldn’t do.”
The wolf-kin muttered amongst themselves, annoyed at my groaning.
“And this is all Rival’s fault, I saaaaaay!”
“I mean, it probably is Gaelion-chan’s doing, but will you seriously never forget this as long as you live, Motoyasu-kun?”
Never, I say, never everrrrr! Later on, the spirit of the spear would tell me, “You know, you do forget plenty of things eventually—but this particular thing, you never forget no matter what.”
“Well, fine. So, next?”
“Next? Hii… I can’t recall, I say.”

As for the Father after that… well, Big Sister was already present, so not much had changed there, except a terrifying Filo-tan went gagagaga—. Deliberately cutting that part out, I say. Moving on from there to the next Father I could recall… that would be the loop where he reunited with Fleon-chan.
“I think something happened around then, from what Gaelion-chan and the others said.”
“T-the next Father’s hobby was peddling, I say.”
Once said, there was no taking it back, but I figured it’d be fine.
“Sounds fun enough, honestly. Buying goods and selling them around… sounds like an enjoyable little life, doesn’t it?”

“To be precise, he was helping rebuild a village, but it seemed more like a way to blow off steam amid the chaos of Amaki going full dark-hero and Itsuki being obsessed with hero activities alongside Fleon-chan.”
“Doesn’t sound all that different from now… or maybe the level of chaos is just different?”
“Probably exhausting having two of them around, right? Bad enough with just one of you.”

Rabbit Guy and Crocodile Guy speculated based on my story. Well, Fiancée had been along for that one too, so— Trash had been causing chaos right alongside them too, I thought, but this was supposed to be about Father’s post-peace-hobbies.
“The Father after that one had a hobby of diving into the sea together with Older Sister. Apparently it was because the ocean floor was so beautiful, I say.”
“Diving, huh—”
“He’d even turn into peckul form and go swimming together with her—that one left an impression, I say.”
Thinking back on it, Father really did have quite the variety of different hobbies across the loops.
“Hey. Was that actually okay?”
“If there weren’t many people around, it might not have been a problem.”
“Going peckul-form with Sadeena-san… that sounds a little scary, honestly, but I guess it shows a lot of trust?”
“Vof.”
“Next?”
“That would be the current Father, I say.”
“Ah, something like that, huh… Makes me think maybe I should try picking up some different hobby myself. Wonder what I should do, though—”
Something to think about, Father said, sounding troubled.
“Can’t mix hobbies and work, though. Well, never mind.”
“You’re already plenty accomplished as it is.”
“Isn’t cooking a hobby?”
“Huh? Cooking? Well, I guess it counts as one, sort of. But Amaki seems to be having fun with it, and if I jumped in too, wouldn’t he just glare at me?”
“Probably.”
Amaki’s cooking was, after all, an imitation of Father and the others’—if the real deal came marching in, there’d be no contest, I say.
“I wouldn’t mind cooking alongside him, but for some reason Amaki hates cooking together with people.”
“Well, Larsazusa’s probably the only one who could ever hope to break into that circle.”
“Ahn? If you worry about every little thing, you won’t get through life, y’know.”
Panda pointed at us with a fork-like utensil while eating.
“You can’t just brush it off like that. Not everyone’s built like you.”
“Well, personally, I hate cooking contests too. Especially the ones where a parent’s reputation gets dragged into it—no thanks, seriously.”
“I don’t think Lars-san’s father would mind, though—”
“That’s not the point, is it? Geez, how long are we gonna keep talking about this?”
“Well, speaking of hobbies—what about grooming? Like a trimmer?”
Father asked me, his face brightening.
“In every single loop, Father took care of everyone’s coats, I say.”
“That one’s a stable, standard-issue trait, I’d say.”
“Honestly, I’d be curious if there’s ever been a different pattern.”
“Vof.”
The slaves all nodded together in agreement, and Father shot them a look of exasperation.
“Hey now. What exactly do you all think of me?”
“Eh? Don’t you like fussing over people’s coats?”
“It’s less about coats and more about… skin, I guess, that sort of area.”
“It’s not that I like it—I just end up noticing, that’s all…”
“Vof.”
Thanks to him, our coats are nice and glossy, the slaves said, showing off their fur.
“Isn’t that just a trait of Shield Hero?”
“Might be.”
“Yeah, yeah, fine, I get it. Let’s drop it, change the subject.”

Father forcibly steered the conversation elsewhere. No doubt he’d been caught dead to rights. Heh, when it comes to usaunny coats, I won’t lose out either, I say. And so, the night wore on in such a manner. The dinner party carried on lively, and in the end, came to a peaceful close.
